REAL ESTATE

30-Year Fixed: 7.46% -0.02  |  15-Year Fixed: 6.98% -0.04

Builders are the gloomiest since 2012. Builder confidence fell four points to 25 in November, the lowest since April 2012, according to the NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index. 46% of builders cut prices, the most since the pandemic, by an average of 6%, and 68% offered incentives. In the West, which includes California, the three month reading fell to 23, the weakest of the four regions.

Here, new homes lost their edge. In our five cities, 10 of 42 homes built in 2025 or 2026 are in contract (24%), the same rate as resale; on October 20 it was 19 of 52 (37%). Across the Bay East board, 21 of 136 new homes are in contract (15%), against 25% for resale. Census figures out this morning show single family permits fell 8.7% in October to a 772,000 annual pace, which NAHB calls the slowest since January 2023.

What it means for you. If you are buying, a builder with finished homes to move is negotiating, so ask for a rate buydown or closing costs before a price cut. If you are selling a resale home, nearby new construction is competing with incentives, so price to today's comps. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.46% this morning, with the 15-year at 6.98%.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,350 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,381 Tuesday, with 132 coming soon and 119 brand new. The five city ledger carries 594 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 530 on the market and 64 coming soon, down from 604.

Fremont holds 200 live listings: 160 active, 24 coming soon and 15 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,288,500 at $783 a square foot and a typical listing out 40 days; with 20% down at 7.46%, that median runs about $7,179 a month in principal and interest. Hayward carries 172, Milpitas 95, Newark 71 and Union City 56. Across all five cities the median is $1,048,371 at $668 a square foot, 259 homes are priced under a million, and 189 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

STOCKS

S&P 500: 7,340.53 -1.03%  |  Dow: 50,759.42 -1.64%  |  Nasdaq: 24,328.38 -0.74%

Tuesday's close, Wednesday's open. The figures above are Tuesday's closes. As of 10:25 AM PT Wednesday the S&P 500 was down 0.05%, the Dow down 0.85% and the Nasdaq up 0.51%.

Nvidia doubled its sales. Santa Clara's Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter ended October 25, up 103% from a year ago, and guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter, its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down, with finance chief Colette Kress serving as interim CEO. The stock slipped 0.44% Tuesday and was down 2.15% at $152.11 this morning.

ECONOMY

10-Year Treasury: 5.10% -0.02  |  Gold: $3,864.20 +0.29%  |  Silver: $47.36 +1.06%  |  Brent Crude: $93.14 +0.76%

A record cycle for political ads. Political advertisers spent a record $12.06 billion in the 2025 to 2026 cycle, according to AdImpact, the first midterm cycle to outspend a presidential one ($11.20 billion in 2024). California led every state at $1.32 billion, the first state ever past $1 billion in a single cycle, and broadcast TV took the biggest share, $5.85 billion.

Shoppers slowed down. Retail sales rose 0.2% in October after 0.8% in September, the Census Bureau reported, a gain too small to rule out no change at all.

Rates and metals. The figures above are Tuesday's settlements. The 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.10%, down 0.02. Gold and silver are sliding this morning, gold down 3.21% near $3,740.30 and silver down 5.11% near $44.94, and Brent is down about 2.2% near $91.11.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Bitcoin: $63,139 -1.20%  |  Ethereum: $1,767.73 -1.44%  |  XRP: $0.98 +2.02%

A quiet day for crypto. Bitcoin is near $63,139, down 1.20% over the past 24 hours, live from CoinGecko at 10:25 AM PT. Ether is near $1,767.73 and XRP near $0.98.
